artists.biography: Longpigs were a British alternative rock band who rose to fame on the fringe of Britpop in the 1990s; comprising Crispin Hunt (vocals), Richard Hawley (guitar), Simon Stafford (bass guitar) and former Cabaret Voltaire member Dee Boyle (drums) who was replaced by Andy Cook (drums) on their second album. Hailing from Sheffield, the group had success with singles such as "She Said", "On and On", and their well-received debut album The Sun Is Often Out (1996).

Longpigs.biography: Longpigs were a British alternative rock band who rose to fame on the fringe of Britpop in the 1990s; comprising Crispin Hunt (vocals), Richard Hawley (guitar), Simon Stafford (bass guitar) and former Cabaret Voltaire member Dee Boyle (drums) who was replaced by Andy Cook (drums) on their second album. Hailing from Sheffield, the group had success with singles such as "She Said", "On and On", and their well-received debut album The Sun Is Often Out (1996).

perplexity.description:
Mobile Home, released in October 1999 on Demon Records, is the second and final studio album by English indie rock band Longpigs. The album continues the band's exploration of alternative and Britpop-influenced rock, blending melodic pop/rock with introspective lyrics and atmospheric arrangements. It features singles such as "Blue Skies" and "The Frank Sonata," which showcase the band's polished sound and Crispin Hunt's distinctive vocals.

Following their well-received debut The Sun Is Often Out (1996), Mobile Home marked a more mature and refined musical direction, incorporating richer production and a broader sonic palette. Although it briefly reached the UK Top 40 albums chart, peaking at number 33, the album did not achieve the same commercial impact as their debut. Critically, it was noted for its solid songwriting and the band's ability to evolve within the Britpop and alternative rock scenes of the late 1990s, though it remained somewhat underappreciated at the time.
